prompt: Design an AI personal trainer app — an adaptive workout coach that builds daily routines, tracks reps sets and personal records, and adjusts your plan as you progress. It needs a home dashboard with today's session and readiness score, a library of guided exercises with form cues, and a progress screen with strength curves and milestones. Make it feel motivating, modern, and personal.
title: Rally Coach

issues.description: The visible SCENES content is abstract SVG artwork rather than a human demonstration image or motion reference. This does not satisfy the guided exercise detail requirement or Airbnb’s photo-first, human-touch direction.

The visible detail navigation identifies the exercise as “Push Up,” while the copy plan defines the focused detail exercise as “Single-arm row.” A single-exercise page must use one consistent item and only that item’s photos, facts, history, and coaching content.
The visible gallery image labels are generic identifiers such as “fitness scene 3076417990,” which do not communicate the exercise, movement phase, or coaching purpose to assistive technology.

The visible shared component uses hardcoded HSL color generation and hardcoded white text for avatars instead of theme tokens. Replace those values with chart or semantic custom properties so the component remains compliant with the token system.
The shared Card component uses a literal rounded-xl class rather than the theme radius scale. Use the configured radius custom property to preserve consistent company styling.

The page is mostly a focused exercise detail, but the Guest reviews section is an unrelated lodging-marketplace pattern. It makes the screen read like an Airbnb listing template rather than a focused secondary workout workflow.
Guest reviews, guest names, star ratings, and review language are not specific to an AI personal trainer and conflict with the product brief.
The required Add to today's session action is missing. The available Start workout action does not satisfy the exercise-library/detail requirement.
The exercise facts and summary card disagree on sets and suggested load: 3 sets and 66 lb versus 4 sets and 44 lb. This undermines trust in the coach.
The gallery is technically scoped to one exercise, but it consists of repetitive abstract illustrations rather than a convincing human form demonstration or useful motion reference.

The exercise detail uses a marketplace-style gallery, reviews, save icon, and search header that closely echo the supplied Airbnb reference. The product target should lead with coaching guidance and exercise utility instead.

The home screen communicates today's session well, but the readiness check is reduced to an 87 score. Sleep quality, energy, soreness, recent strain, and the resulting plain-language recommendation are not present.
The required progress and milestone workflow is absent: there is no strength curve, recent personal records, weekly consistency visualization, or concrete milestone.
The top metric band contains three nested cards in addition to a six-card exercise grid, exceeding the intended scarce-card system. Stats should be rendered as a band or divided stat row.
Heart icons and star ratings on exercise cards appear to be listing/review affordances copied from the inspiration template. They do not communicate workout status, effort, or progression.

The lower half has oversized whitespace and sparse sections around Readiness score, Coach insight, and After workout. The page loses momentum after the workout grid instead of presenting a clear progress and adjustment story.
Several adjacent lower sections use the same white surface with limited visual separation. The vertical rhythm and surface alternation are weaker than the required composed section system.

The product is described as mobile-first, but the visible composition is a wide desktop three-column grid with no evidence that the dominant workout action, readiness controls, and exercise logging remain prioritized at mobile width.

reviewResult.summary: The implementation has a fitness-relevant foundation and uses several shared components, token-based colors, and an appropriately warm rounded visual direction. Approval is blocked by the detail workflow: its visible gallery is abstract rather than human exercise guidance, and the exercise identity is inconsistent between navigation and the prescribed detail content. Shared component token violations also need cleanup.
requiredFixes: In src/screens/detail.jsx, replace the abstract generated SVG scene gallery with a human exercise demonstration image or motion reference for the single-arm row. Use 4–5 visually consistent images of that same exercise, with exercise-specific accessible labels.

In src/screens/detail.jsx, make the detail identity consistent with the product brief: the page, gallery, navigation label, facts, and actions must all describe one exercise, preferably “Single-arm row,” rather than mixing it with “Push Up” or “Push-up tempo.”

In src/screens/home.jsx, ensure the dominant moment is the adaptive “Today's workout” workflow, with the session goal, duration, ordered exercises, target sets/reps, suggested loads, one-sentence coach adjustment, and one clear “Start session” action visible before secondary progress content.
detail: Replace the Airbnb-style Guest reviews section with exercise-specific content such as common mistakes, target muscles, equipment, and a divided form-cue list.
detail: Add a prominent "Add to today's session" action to the single exercise summary area; do not use only "Start workout."
detail: Correct the conflicting workout data: the page shows 3 sets and 66 lb in the exercise facts but 4 sets, 10 reps, and 44 lb in the summary card.
detail: Use a human demonstration image or a clearly authored motion-reference sequence for Push-up tempo, rather than five near-identical abstract gallery crops.

home: Remove Airbnb/template residue such as heart-save controls, star ratings, and review-like scores from workout cards; replace them with completion state, last-session comparison, or perceived effort.
home: Add the required readiness check inputs for sleep, energy, soreness, and recent training strain, each with visible labels and mobile-appropriate controls.
home: Convert the three top metrics into a single tonal stats band instead of nested cards, and reduce the total card count to preserve card discipline.
home: Add the required progress and milestone section with a legible branded strength curve, recent personal records, weekly consistency, and a concrete milestone.
home: Tighten the large empty gaps around Readiness score, Coach insight, and After workout, and give adjacent sections alternating surfaces and deliberate rhythm.
